title: RowActionsMenu
wrapsNative: A ghost icon Button and a popover of text Buttons (a shortcut hint at the end of a row, a danger row after a MonarchDivider) with confirmationDialog for destructive items; Menu with Button items and .menuStyle(.button) remains the choice for the system menu
summary: The per-row actions of a list or table are the standard SwiftUI Menu behind a "⋯" button, swipe actions and a context menu, with destructive items last. Monarch ships nothing; the trigger takes the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: For the actions on one row, card or item: a "⋯" Menu that is always visible, swipeActions for the one or two most frequent actions on List rows, and contextMenu (press and hold) with the full set.
whenNotToUse: For actions on several selected rows, use MonarchBulkActionBar. For a single obvious action, put a button on the row. For screen-level actions, use the navigation bar's toolbar.
api: Button(_ title: String, systemImage: String, role: ButtonRole? = nil, action: () -> Void)
func swipeActions<T: View>(edge: HorizontalEdge = .trailing, allowsFullSwipe: Bool = true, content: () -> T) -> some View
func contextMenu<MenuItems: View>(menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View
func confirmationDialog(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: open
states.description: The system draws the menu next to the "⋯" button.

states.name: swiped
states.description: On a List row, swiping from the trailing edge reveals the swipe buttons; a full swipe runs the first one.

states.name: destructive
states.description: A Button with role: .destructive is drawn in the system's red, sits last after a Divider, and asks for confirmation before it runs.

states.name: disabled
states.description: An item with disabled(true) is dimmed; disable the trigger to block every action.

appearance: The menu, swipe buttons and context menu are drawn by the system in every theme and follow light, dark and Increase Contrast. The "⋯" trigger is a small ghost MonarchButtonStyle button. Swipe buttons take tint(_:) for a non-destructive colour; destructive ones are the system red.
platformNotes: The web RowActionsMenu is a component that sorts danger items to the end and opens a ConfirmDialog for items with `confirm`. On iOS the app lists the items in that order with a Divider before the destructive ones and presents confirmationDialog itself, so Monarch adds no type. iOS adds swipe actions and a context menu, which the web does not have; use the same items in all three. The web shortcut hint is keyboardShortcut on the Button, shown by the system with a hardware keyboard. Android plans a Compose recipe for the same menu.
accessibility: Name the icon-only trigger after the row ("Actions for Acme Ltd") with the Label's title, so rows are told apart.
System behaviour: swipe actions and context-menu items are offered to VoiceOver in the rotor's Actions on the row.
System behaviour: destructive items are announced with their role, and the confirmation dialog takes focus.
The trigger keeps a 44-point touch target through MonarchButtonStyle.
edgeCases: Swipe actions only work on rows of a List; on other stacks use the "⋯" Menu and contextMenu.
Set allowsFullSwipe: false when the first swipe action is destructive and must be confirmed.
A destructive item that runs at once after a full swipe should offer Undo (see undo-toast) instead of a confirmation.
